target_customer: Engineering, platform and security teams running production services, mostly on Kubernetes, in mid-size and large enterprises
problem: Distributed tracing and OpenTelemetry instrumentation require code changes and per-language setup, so adoption was low. Odigos instruments applications automatically using eBPF and OpenTelemetry without code changes.
business_model: Open source core with a commercial platform and 14-day trial
product_category: OpenTelemetry auto-instrumentation and observability control plane

founders.name: Eden Federman
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch calls him an Israeli developer and active open source contributor in the eBPF and OpenTelemetry communities.

founders.name: Ari Recht
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch describes him as an investment banker who does not code; employer not named.

technical_complexity.rationale: Automatic instrumentation across languages using eBPF and runtime injection into running applications is deep systems engineering for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Open source adoption and language coverage give some advantage, but eBPF instrumentation was also being built by Grafana, Pixie and others, and later became an OpenTelemetry project.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Grafana donated Beyla to OpenTelemetry, where it became OBI with a first alpha in November 2025, with Odigos among contributors per a secondary source; Odigos remained independent.

market_need_then: TechCrunch says the CTO saw low adoption of distributed tracing, and OpenTelemetry was growing as a vendor neutral standard.

branding.name_origin: TechCrunch says the company was initially named Keyval; no source explains Odigos. The Greek word for guide is odigos but no source ties the name to it.
branding.community_and_virality: Open source project and OpenTelemetry community presence; founders maintain Go auto-instrumentation per YC page.

brand_strength.rationale: Distinct name with developer community presence, but no press about the brand itself found.

pivots.to: Production context platform for observability, security and coding agents
pivots.why: Not stated; the shift is visible by comparing the company's earlier coverage and its current homepage

outcome_analysis: Odigos raised a SAFE around YC Demo Day and a $13M round in September 2024 led by Venture Guides with Salesforce Ventures, and now lists customers such as T-Mobile and Merck. An open source, vendor neutral approach rode the OpenTelemetry wave, but eBPF instrumentation is also being built by larger vendors and standards bodies.
notes: The $13M round is labeled Series A by databases and seed by others; TechCrunch gives no label, so stage is other. The earlier SAFE amount and date are not stated; recorded without an amount, dated 2023 around YC Demo Day. CB Insights reports $13.5M total, unverified. Headquarters reported inconsistently (Boston, Tel Aviv). Datadog, Dynatrace, SigNoz and Honeycomb are named by TechCrunch in 2024 as tools Odigos works alongside, not as dated 2023 competitors, so the list is empty. The pivot entry is a loose description of product positioning, date unknown.
